title: Calendar And Rebalance Mechanics
market_behavior: Scheduled rebalances, month-end flows, option expirations, and fund reporting windows can create predictable trading pressure.
forced_actor: Index products, asset allocators, target-date funds, option hedgers, and funds managing benchmark or reporting constraints.
why_edge_might_exist: Some trading is caused by calendar mechanics rather than updated expected returns, so pressure may be predictable around known windows.
why_large_capital_may_ignore_it: Many calendar effects are small, crowded, timing-sensitive, and fragile after execution costs; niche versions may be capacity-limited.
capacity_hypothesis: Capacity may be moderate in broad ETFs and lower in niche instruments; edge should be assumed small until measured with realistic execution.
data_required: daily or intraday price data depending on event timing
flow or positioning proxies where available
observable_predictions: Returns or volatility differ around prespecified calendar windows after controlling for broad market movement.
Effects should survive being defined entirely before the test period.
falsification_tests: Reject if date windows are tuned after seeing returns.
Reject if realistic costs remove the edge.
Treat intraday-specific mechanics as blocked until intraday data exists.
references: Index and fund rebalance methodology documents
